registered: 2026-10-29 (before the registered run; written after the lifter spec/lift/python/lift_py.py was developed against the corpus, see 'development')
question: Critique 8 and RJ-F1 of the RCE-JEPA page ('Lift coverage plateaus below 80% on any of the five target languages after the construct list is exhausted'): how much real Python does the first lifter of the RCE project carry exactly into RCE text, and what blocks the rest?

instrument.lifter: spec/lift/python/lift_py.py of openIE-dev/rce branch claude/lift-python (stdlib ast only; route T of spec/proposals/rce-form.md section 16; runtime spec/lift/python/runtime.rce). The run uses commit 5583974e of that branch, frozen for the run: no change to the lifter, its runtime or its rules between this registration and the run, other than an amendment registered here before a second run.
instrument.harness: spec/lift/python/verify_lift.py RCE OUT (whole programs) and spec/lift/python/coverage.py RCE FILE (functions), same commit
instrument.reference: rce built from openIE-dev/rce main 8ce91cea (the lifter changes no Rust), release build
instrument.oracle: the recorded observations of lang/python3.13/corpus (CPython 3.13.16, rce-obs/1, command profile), never re-derived from the lift

population.real_world_primary: heapq.py of the pinned CPython 3.13.16 standard library (/usr/lib/python3.13/heapq.py, a file of the oracle record's pinned tree, sha256 6d43277e5c76fc0f073cd388fcff852d14d068f6bb6d4886c340f8b75a1229a9): a small pure-Python module written for use, not as a benchmark

outcomes.per_case: exactly one of MATCH (lift applied; exit status, stdout bytes and stderr class equal the recorded observation), MATCH-RESOURCE (class resource, the lifted program kept its event at a resource limit: holds by section 20), DIFFERS (lift applied, observations differ: a lifter defect, reported with the first differing byte), KEPT-RESOURCE (lift applied, the lifted program trapped at a limit, i64 overflow, a loop or recursion bound, where CPython answered: never counted as holding), REQUIRES-CHANGE (the lift reported constructs outside the subset with their rules), INTERNAL (the lifted text fails rce check, or rce run fails or does not end within 120 s)
outcomes.per_function: for every def of the module (module level and nested defs counted where ast finds a module-level def): lifted (the function and every function it calls lift and the printed text passes rce check), or requires change with every rule named; a function is never counted as lifted when a callee requires change (rule L-PY-CALLEE)
outcomes.breakdown: counts of cases (and of functions) naming each rule, the rule of the first line reported, and the cases whose only rule is that rule

primary_metrics.real_world_function_coverage: lifted functions / all functions of heapq.py

predictions.corpus: MATCH + MATCH-RESOURCE at most 15 of 92: the corpus programs were written to exercise one construct family each, including exceptions, classes, floats, sets, generators and imports that the subset leaves out, and most programs combine several
predictions.heapq: function coverage below 20%: the functions are polymorphic over the item type (no call in the module fixes it) and the sift loops have no bound derivable by the closed rule list
predictions.rj_f1: the measured coverage is far below 80%; it is a first measurement and not a plateau, since the construct list (the rules L-PY-*) is not exhausted, so RJ-F1 is reported as neither met nor refuted by this run

development: The lifter was written and debugged against the 92 corpus cases (they are the acceptance suite of section 20; there is no held-out part of the corpus, and a case that differs is fixed in the lifter, rule K4). Before this registration the functions mode was run once on heapq.py to check that it reports every function (0 lifted); after that run only the wording of diagnostics changed (bound methods and keyword-only parameters were named under the right rule), no rule of what lifts. The secondary modules were not run before registration.
exclusions: none: every case and every function is reported
reporting: RESULTS.md with the rce commit, the counts, the breakdown, and the RJ-F1 line; results/verify.txt (the harness output), results/coverage-*.txt, results/summary.json

amendments.after: the registered run at 5583974e (results/verify.txt, results/coverage-*.txt, results/corpus-functions.txt, kept as recorded); before the second run
amendments.why: the run found one lifter defect: the descriptive function-level run over the corpus printed text for matrix.py's mul that rce check does not accept (INTERNAL: sum() of a generator inside a comprehension bound a temporary outside the comprehension). Reading the code for that defect found two more of the same family (temporaries bound before a while test, a branch, an and/or operand; an elif test discarding the if test's temporaries) and an order dependence of type inference (a call written after a function did not fix the parameter types before the function's methods were resolved).
amendments.change: openIE-dev/rce claude/lift-python commit eb2cd4e5 fixes these; nothing else in the rules of what lifts changes
amendments.second_run: the same population, outcomes and metrics at eb2cd4e5, recorded under results/v2/; RESULTS.md reports both runs, the registered one first
